samples.summary: `parseColumnWidthsAttr` turns an absent/empty `cols` attribute from one zero-ratio column into zero columns, so such a table lays out no cells at all
samples.evidence: The replaced expression `(attrs.cols ?? '').split(',').map(Number).filter((n) => !isNaN(n))` yields `[0]` for a missing/empty attribute (`''.split(',') === ['']`, `Number('') === 0`), i.e. `columnWidths.length === 1`. `parseColumnWidthsAttr` returns `[]` for a falsy attr. `computeTableLayout` uses `const numCols = columnWidths.length` (`packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:153`) for its cell loops, so such a table now lays out zero cells (content invisible) instead of one degenerate column. Same change at the second boundary, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:475`. Only reachable for a table node written without `cols`, which today's serializer always emits — hence minor.

verdict.reason: The slides store applies the new `bandBlockNumerics` guard on its read/write text paths (yorkie-slides-store.ts:529, 2253, 2300), but the board store — an explicitly documented verbatim port — reads and rewrites the same kind of stored `Block[]` with no band: yorkie-board-store.ts:374 (readElement), :1319 (withTextElement), :1351 (withShapeText). Those elements flow through read() (:311-328) into boardToSlidesDocument (packages/board/src/model/board.ts:42-74), which is a pure single-slide wrapper performing no normalization, and then into the shared slides/docs layout engine. A repo-wide grep shows bandBlockNumerics exists only in packages/docs (definition/export/tests), the slides store, and review artifacts — nothing in packages/board/src (no band/sanitize/normalize matches at all) or the frontend board directory, and named-styles.ts only bands the stylesJson registry, not stored block/inline numerics. So a peer writing fontSize: 1e9 or rowSpan: Infinity into a board text/sticky element still reaches computeLayout unbanded — the exact bypass this change exists to close. No counterexample found.

The docs preview is safe (`parseDocsSnapshot` → `docsTreeToDocument`, banded by this change); the slides/board preview is the reader of the same stored bytes left out. verdict.reason: The slides/board revision-preview path is genuinely unbanded end-to-end. `parseSlidesSnapshot` (snapshot-adapters.ts:44-46) and `parseBoardSnapshot` (:61-76) apply only `unwrapYsonScalars`, which by its own contract changes nothing but CRDT scalar wrappers (unwrap-yson.ts:88-108). The result goes straight into `new MemSlidesStore(doc)` (revision-preview.tsx:582), whose constructor and `read()` only call `migrateDocument` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:140-157) — migrate.ts has finite checks only for pxPerPt/slideHeight/guide positions. The renderer does not recover it: `prepareBlocksForLayout` applies only `normalizeBlockStyle` (text-renderer.ts:258-268), which is a bare spread (docs/src/model/types.ts:382-384), before `computeLayout` (:239,:299); the docs layout engine bands nothing but table rowHeights (table-layout.ts:256). A repo-wide grep for every band symbol (bandBlockNumerics, normalizeFontSize/LineHeight/CellPadding/TableSpan/ColumnRatio/RowHeight, isPaintableImageSize) returns zero hits in packages/slides/src, packages/board/src and packages/frontend/src/components/history — the bands live only in docs' crdt-tree codec (which is why parseDocsSnapshot is safe) and in the live yorkie-slides-store read paths. numeric-attrs.ts:267-292 states explicitly that slide text bodies are persisted/read verbatim and need this band on read. The preview is reachable in the product (document-detail.tsx:700 and sibling detail overlays; tests render type="slides"/"board" at revision-preview.test.tsx:166,178). So this is a read-boundary guard with a second reader around it — in-lane and blocking.

finding.summary: The new slides numeric band exists only on the v1 REST `PUT`; the collaborative Yorkie path reads/writes slide text bodies unbanded
finding.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `bandSlideCellNumerics` / the inline `fontSize` band were added to `assertValidSlidesBody` (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1001-1078`), whose own doc-comment says a slide text body "passes through no attribute codec" so the band must happen on write. But the REST endpoint is not the only writer or reader: `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:494-512` materializes a text element as `data: { ...extras, blocks }` with `blocks = yorkieToPlain(data.blocks)` — no `normalizeFontSize` / `normalizeTableSpan` / `normalizeRowHeight` anywhere in that file — and the slides editor writes bodies straight back through the same store. A peer (or any client) writing `fontSize: 1e9` or `rowSpan: Infinity` into `el.data.blocks` never passes the controller, and those blocks are fed to the shared docs layout (`computeLayout`, docs `initializeTextBox`, `expandCellRangeForMerges` for cell selection). Unlike docs, where the same band is duplicated at both read boundaries (`crdt-tree.ts` and `yorkie-doc-store.ts`), slides has no read-side copy. The fix belongs on the slides read boundary, not on the new controller code.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the slides Yorkie read boundary has no numeric band ("no normalizeFontSize / normalizeTableSpan / normalizeRowHeight anywhere in that file"), leaving peer-written fontSize/rowSpan unbanded. The code is not as described. yorkie-slides-store.ts:65 imports `bandBlockNumerics` from `@wafflebase/docs`, and the exact read path the finding cites applies it: :529-531 bands `blocks` before building `data: { ...extras, blocks }` at :546. A dedicated helper `bandElementText` (:485-513) bands shape text (:502) and every table cell body (:510), and is invoked on the generic element read path at :608; notes are banded at :435. The three named normalizers are reached through that shared helper: packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:320 (normalizeFontSize), :339 (normalizeRowHeight), :363-371 (normalizeTableSpan for colSpan/rowSpan, with a comment naming the expandCellRangeForMerges loop the finding cites), recursing into nested cell blocks at :372-374. The reviewer appears to have grepped for the normalizer names literally and missed the shared band function that calls them; the premise that the v1 PUT is the only bander is contradicted by the in-file comment at :494-495 and by the call sites above. Ground: not-present.
